topics.definition: A tree is a non-linear data structure consisting of nodes connected by edges in a hierarchical manner.
Common terms include Root, Parent, Child, Sibling, Leaf, Height and Depth.
topics.example: A is the root, B is the child.
tips: Learn the terminology before tree algorithms.

topics.definition: A binary tree is a tree in which each node has at most two children.
tips: Each node has at most two children.

topics.definition: A BST is a binary tree where left child values are smaller and right child values are larger than the parent.
tips: Searching is efficient in a balanced BST.

topics.definition: Traversal visits all tree nodes in a specific order.
tips: Inorder traversal of a BST gives sorted output.

topics.definition: Visits nodes level by level using a queue.
Trees are used in file systems, databases, expression trees and decision making.
tips: BSTs and heaps are common in software.

topics.definition: Trees provide efficient searching and hierarchical storage but are more complex than arrays.
Typical programs include insertion, deletion, searching and traversals.
